data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's refusal condition is over-broad relative to its own exceptions. The claim states resumption 'must be refused whenever budget state and event log are coupled in the same append-only structure, unless the budget-exhaustion record is written via a separate out-of-band channel.' This 'unless' clause enumerates only one escape condition. Yet the target's own counterconditions identify at least four other conditions under which coupled budget-and-log would still permit safe resumption: (2) reserving budget for the halt-marker event, (3) harness-level budget control below the event log, (4) optional halt marker whose absence is not corruption, and (5) two-phase commit leaving a recoverable prepared marker. Because the refusal clause names only the out-of-band channel as the exception, it would mandate refusing resumption in every coupled architecture except one, even though the target itself acknowledges those other coupled architectures are safe. The stated refusal condition is thus not the 'precise' condition the problem demands.
